column2: Slipping past the hesitating Mr. Kobayashi, I went on into the room.
Shivering in the cold wind, I made my way toward the back.
Suddenly I spotted something strange at my feet.
It looked like a crumpled-up piece of memo paper.
When I bent down to pick it up, I noticed something red smeared all over the paper.
Careful not to touch it, I picked the paper up by the tips of my fingers and unfolded it.
{n2} and Mr. Kobayashi peered over my shoulder from behind.
Something odd was written on it.
It looks like a poem, but…”
When I muttered that, Mr. Kobayashi's face changed.
Afraid he might have collapsed somewhere, I frantically started searching the room.
I looked under the bed, in the bathroom and, just in case, even inside the closet.
then he must be badly hurt.{r}{p}And he escaped out the window…?”
Mr. Kobayashi went to the window and stuck his head out into the blizzard.
“Anyway, let's get out of here for now.{r}{p}It's way too cold in here.”
We readily went along with {n2}'s suggestion.
We went downstairs with the people who had been peeking in from the hallway and settled into the common room.
So everyone could see it, I spread the mysterious memo out on the table.
Everyone craned their necks to look.
“…I don't know.{r}{p}This is all that was left.{r}{p}It seems to be a hint to where some treasure is, but…”
Are you saying there's buried gold or something near this inn?”
Midori snorted, as if the whole thing were ridiculous.
“…Maybe.{r}{p}Maybe it's not buried treasure, just ordinary money or jewels…{r}{p}Whatever it is, that Tanaka guy vanished and left this behind.{r}{p}Judging by the blood,
there was definitely some kind of fight.{r}{p}If so, the most plausible explanation is that a real treasure exists and his partners fell out over it.”
even so, I don't know about the treasure, or whatever it is, being in the 'Spur'…{r}{p}Why would something like that even be
I spoke as I thought it through.

say the culprits who stole some jewels and fled hid out here for a while.{r}{p}Before parting ways, they hid the jewels somewhere in this building.{r}{p}Then a year later, one of them came back to retrieve them, calling himself Tanaka…”
“Think about it: if that Tanaka guy had hidden the treasure himself, he wouldn't need a memo like that.{r}{p}He was carrying it because he didn't know the hiding place, right?”
True.{r}{p}Then maybe Tanaka wasn't one of the gang. Maybe he got hold of a memo one of the criminals had and tried to snatch the loot.{r}{p}But they found out and caught him…”
“Forget the guessing.{r}{p}Anyway, we just have to solve this hint, right?{r}{p}Then we'll know right away whether there's really any treasure…
Let me take a good look at it.”
“…Let's see… 'Between 1 and 3'?{r}{p}That's obviously 2.{r}{p}So it's somewhere on the second floor.”
“All right, the second floor it is!”
The moment he heard that, Mr. Kayama jumped to his feet.
The two of them bolted like startled hares,
I scrambled to my feet and followed the Kayamas
The Kayamas were looking around the hallway, unsure where to go.
They seemed to be wondering which door to try.
Haruko pointed to the room of that Tanaka fellow.
Seeing the two of them burst inside, the rest of us rushed the doorway too.
While the rest of us dithered, the Kayamas searched the closet, the bathroom and under the bed, one after another.
But after a while, Mr. Kayama cried out with a sigh.
The instant they heard his voice,
the people behind me scattered, running off to their own rooms.
They seemed to have decided to search their own rooms thoroughly first.
I hurried back to my own room too.
I went over every spot that looked like it could hide something.
But there was nothing out of the ordinary.
I wondered how everyone else was doing….
When I stepped into the hallway, everyone was coming out looking disappointed.
Apparently there was nothing on the second floor after all.
“Let's take another look at that memo.”
We all nodded at {n2}'s words and went back to the common room.
It couldn't be in my own room, I thought.
My eyes settled on the storeroom at the end of the hallway.
I waited until everyone had disappeared from the hallway, then ran to the storeroom door.
I took one deep breath and threw the double doors wide open.
With a loud crash, something lunged at me!
Screaming, I flailed both arms at the shadow attacking me.
But in an instant, some tremendous force had knocked me flat.
“Why are you buried under mops and brooms?”
The tightly packed brooms had simply toppled over onto me.
From under the brooms, I apologized to the people who had come running in alarm.
Apparently nothing had turned up on the second floor, so we went back down to the common room to go over the memo again.
“Come on, calm down.{r}{p}There's still plenty written on the back.”
I put on a composed air.
'The road to Hades'?{r}{p}What's that supposed to mean?”
“But the part after that doesn't make any sense.”
The second floor or the basement.{r}{p}We might learn something if we just go look, right?”
She seemed worried that the Kayamas would find it first.
Then let's try the second floor.”
A tremendous clatter and crash echoed down from the second floor.
What we saw when we raced up the stairs…
was the Kayamas, struggling under a pile of brooms and mops.
They must have tried to search the storeroom at the end of the hallway and gotten buried.
We all moved the brooms and pulled them out, and Mr. Kayama spoke as if blaming Mr. Kobayashi.
“Packin' it that full is dangerous, y'know?{r}{p}I nearly suffocated!”
I asked, holding back a laugh.
“Nah, doesn't look like it's on the second floor.{r}{p}And if it's not the second floor…
We watched them dash off in a daze.
We trooped back to the common room and decided to go over the memo again.
With Mr. Kobayashi in the lead, we all headed for the basement.
Just as Mr. Kobayashi was unlocking the door, we heard pounding footsteps, and the Kayamas came running down.
Overwhelmed by his intensity, Mr. Kobayashi meekly opened the door and stepped aside.
Mr. Kayama, already at full speed, flew straight through the doorway, and then…
he went tumbling down the stairs into the darkness.
A rumbling thud echoed up from below.
With Mr. Kobayashi in the lead, we hurried down the stairs
Mr. Kayama lay sprawled out on the floor below.
Mr. Kobayashi went over and put a hand on his chest.
Just unconscious.{r}{p}Let's carry him to his room.{r}{p}…Toshio, give me a hand.”
The two of them hoisted Mr. Kayama up and climbed the narrow stairs.
The rest of us followed them back to the first floor.
That was when I suddenly noticed something.
I don't see the girls anywhere.”
They were here a minute ago.
Only Mr. Kobayashi, Toshio and Haruko had gone up to the second floor with Mr. Kayama.
Yet now there were only me, {n2}, Midori and Kyoko here.
As we looked around, three of them came creeping up the basement stairs.
At my question, the girls exchanged glances.
doesn't seem to be down there.”
Keiko said, then clapped a hand over her mouth.
Apparently the three of them had been secretly searching the basement.
They hadn't forgotten the treasure hunt even after seeing Mr. Kayama; that took real guts.
We were back in the common room, poring over the memo, when Mr. Kobayashi and the others came down.
To my surprise, even Mr. Kayama came down, unsteady on his feet.
I asked, and Mr. Kobayashi answered with a wry smile.
“Well, he insisted on continuing no matter what.”
I was beyond stunned, and impressed.
anyway, show me that memo again, will ya?”
I turned the memo toward Mr. Kayama.
Whether from pain or thought, Mr. Kayama growled like a guard dog.
I peered at it from beside him.
Calmly, I looked over the memo once more.
doesn't necessarily have to mean this place, does it?”
there are no quotation marks around it, right?{r}{p}So maybe it isn't the name of this inn, but a real ski track.{r}{p}A real ski track in the snow.”
“…But a treasure in a ski track? Isn't that strange?”
“It is, but if it's in the ski tracks, doesn't that mean it's on the slopes?{r}{p}Then 'between 1 and 3' would mean Slope 2.”
It must be.{r}{p}I can't believe someone could have hidden a treasure somewhere in the inn without anyone knowing.”
And on the slopes, burying something in the ground would be easy. It was exactly what a criminal would do.
In that case, maybe that Tanaka guy was taken to the slopes.”
“But… if it's the slopes, what about 'Hades'?”
“Probably the danger zone.{r}{p}Get careless and you're dead and off to the other world.”
Near the danger zone on Slope 2….
Still, the text after that made no sense at all.
“And tell them what?{r}{p}'There are people going to dig up treasure buried on the slopes, so arrest them'?”
“We can't do that without any solid evidence.”
“But if that Tanaka guy was taken against his will, he might get killed once they find the treasure…”
“But this scrap of paper and some blood aren't enough to say it's connected to a crime.{r}{p}Mr. Tanaka might have just been doodling, and this blood could be a nosebleed.”
I hadn't even considered that, but it wasn't impossible.
“Then should the rest of us go look for Mr. Tanaka on the slopes?”
When I said that, Mr. Kobayashi and Toshio both shook their heads.
“No way. Heading out to the slopes now, in this weather?{r}{p}…We'd better not.{r}{p}The memo's half-baked, and it's highly doubtful that interpretation from earlier is even right.”
floor, the Kayamas came down looking sour.
“Hey, let me see that paper one more time.”
At Mr. Kayama's request, I turned the paper toward him.
Mr. Kayama glared at the paper for a while, then suddenly cried out.
The basement! It was the basement all along! Haruko, let's go!”
took off running again, vanishing down
Stunned, we watched them go, then turned back to the mysterious memo.
Mr. Kobayashi, is there a well anywhere around here?”
“We used to use well water too,
but with a hand pump. I don't recall ever seeing what you'd call a proper well around here.”
“I mean, the image in a mirror is 'your lookalike'.”
“Then what does it mean to find it 'quicker than your lookalike'?”
I don't know, but maybe it's hidden behind a mirror or something.”
It didn't all add up, but somehow it felt like a plausible hiding place.
Toshio seemed to think so too.
“…There can't be that many mirrors.{r}{p}It might not be it, but why don't we all check our own rooms?”
With that, he headed off to his own room.
The rest of us hurriedly got up and went to our rooms too.
Everyone was back in the common room, dispirited.
Only Mr. Kobayashi was grinning to himself.
If there were a gimmick like that behind a mirror, you think I wouldn't know about it?”
Still, it was a bit mean of Mr. Kobayashi not to have said so until now.
We were at a dead end.
It didn't look like we could squeeze any more meaning out of those words.
“Well, it's a kind of code, sure.”
“That's not what I mean. I'm saying maybe the individual words don't mean anything.”
Maybe if you rearrange the sentences or swap letters around following some rule, you get different words.”
Because at first glance, the text reads as if it points to where the treasure is.
But since some parts made no sense, it seemed worth a try.
We put our heads together again and peered at the mysterious memo.
“Let me take a good look at the memo again.”
“Look as many times as you like.”
It's easy.{r}{p}I must've been out of it not to notice something so simple.”
“So where on earth is the treasure?”
Mr. Kayama demanded, so fiercely he nearly strangled me.
Why outside?{r}{p}It clearly says to scour inside the Spur.{r}{p}Or does it mean something else?”
Actually, I just said the first thing that came to mind.”
When I rattled off places at random, {n2} sighed deeply.
“You don't even know what kind of treasure it is, so we can't exactly search the whole inn, can we?{r}{p}If you don't understand the memo, there's no way to find it.”
“Let's quit this pointless business and go to bed.{r}{p}It's late anyway.”
Only then did I realize it was already past eleven.
Treasure, they say, but it probably turns out to be worthless once you find it.”
Toshio started saying such things too.
Everyone's enthusiasm seemed to have cooled all at once.
I noticed I was terribly tired too.
If I didn't get a good night's sleep, I might not survive the training {n2} surely had in store for me tomorrow.
One after another, everyone stood up and said good night.
“Hey, you're all giving up already?{r}{p}Doesn't this bloodstain bother you?”
Only Mr. Kobayashi tried to hold everyone back.
I led the way and walked into the dining room.
“Hey, {n1}.{r}{p}Didn't you know where it was when you came here?{r}{p}Was it a lie that you solved the memo?”
Aki was looking at the clock.
“We're going to bed.{r}{p}If you find the treasure, show us tomorrow, okay?
The three office ladies went back to their room.
Everyone drifted out of the dining room too.
“I'm gettin' sleepy too.{r}{p}Haruko, shall we head back to the room…?”
Mr. Kayama's voice, speaking as he climbed the stairs, echoed through the hall.
“…When I was young, I could stay up five days straight and be fine….”
Everyone's enthusiasm seemed to have cooled all at once.
“I think I'll go to bed too.{r}{p}It's late anyway.”
Treasure, they say, but it probably turns out to be worthless once you find it.”
Toshio started saying such things too.
The remaining people said good night to one another.
You're all giving up already?{r}{p}Doesn't this bloodstain bother you?”
Only Mr. Kobayashi tried to hold everyone back.
“He's probably out night skiing.{r}{p}Won't he be back eventually?”
“Uncle, if you want to look for him, why don't you look by yourself? Sorry, but we're going to bed.”
One after another everyone left, and finally {n2} and I went up to the second floor.
For some reason, Mr. Kobayashi was watching us with a reproachful look.
Some with bloodshot eyes, some half-doubting….
“Where in this room could something like that possibly be?”
Mr. Kobayashi asked in an oddly quiet voice.
You're not suggesting we tear up the floorboards, are you?”
I mean, isn't there a storage space or something in the floor?{r}{p}You know, like part of the floor opens up….”
What made you think of that?”
It didn't seem to be under the floor.
Mr. Kayama quickly dropped to his hands and knees and peered under the sofa.
aren't you just saying whatever comes to mind?”
Actually, yeah.{r}{p}I haven't got a clue what the memo means.”
Everyone looked up at the ceiling in unison.
I stood up and approached the wall.
I lifted my face and stared at the cuckoo clock.
I reached out, opened the little door the cuckoo pops out of, stood on tiptoe, and peeked inside.
Something like a small pouch was wedged into the gap.
I stuck my fingers in and pulled it out.
Everyone jumped up in surprise and rushed over to me.
It was a small leather pouch.
I untied the cord holding it shut and shook the contents into my palm.
Red and green jewels sparkled brightly.
Mixed in with the jewels was a tightly folded piece of paper.
It looks like you solved the riddle.
this means I can keep these jewels?”
I never imagined I'd actually get a treasure.
wait just a minute, now.{r}{p}We all searched for this together, didn't we? Keepin' it all to yourself is a bit…”
Haruko cut off the flustered Mr. Kayama sharply.
“Dear, you're embarrassing yourself.{r}{p}Besides, we didn't even solve the riddle.”
I'd thought she always obeyed her husband, but in the end the wife seemed to be the stronger one.
“…By the way, how did you know it was there?”
“It's really simple.{r}{p}I just read it vertically.”
“Vertically? S, G, G, S, S… that doesn't spell anything!”
“It's the second letter.{r}{p}You read the second letter of each line, vertically.”

In the cuckoo clock!{r}{p}Oh, is that all?

“Don't be a sore loser.{r}{p}You could just
Is he going to spin some weird logic again to get a share…?
“I know a jeweler, so I thought I could sell 'em for you…”
{n2} paused for a moment, then answered casually.
“This letter I just read? I actually skipped the very end.{r}{p}There's a postscript.
'P.S. All of this, however, is nothing but glass beads.
Total value: three hundred fifty yen.
Everyone except Mr. Kobayashi raised their voices.
I'd had some suspicions, so the glass beads didn't shock me that much.
After all, there was no way a story that good could be real.
But the signature at the end did surprise me.
It was all I could manage to say.
Mr. Kobayashi scratched his head and apologized.
“Well, yes, actually.{r}{p}It was meant as a little entertainment, but it seems everyone took it more seriously than I expected, and I feel a bit bad about it.”
“I had a lot of fun, so it's fine.
…Of course, there's no way a story that good could be real…
In front of {n2}, I laughed to show I could take it.
The laughter drained away from his voice.
They're fakes?{r}{p}Well, 'course they are.{r}{p}Sure they are.
Of course they're fakes.{r}{p}Heh heh heh…
Mr. Kayama's laughter, on the other hand, grew happier and happier.
the fact is, I love making codes like this.{r}{p}I've made others too, reading the third letter vertically, or the fourth, all sorts.{r}{p}I'm sure you've come across a few somewhere…”
Mr. Kobayashi said proudly, but nobody was listening.

that was all part of the act, of course.{r}{p}He's a friend of mine.{r}{p}I had him secretly hide in my room.”
“I'll go get him, and we'll all have a drink together.”
Mr. Kobayashi headed toward the back.
Once Mr. Kobayashi was out of sight, Kyoko murmured with a little giggle.
“What a nuisance.{r}{p}Leaving traces of blood and everything.”
“Well, true, but it was kind of fun, so no harm done.{r}{p}And nobody was actually hurt…”
Just as Midori was saying this,
Mr. Kobayashi came running back in a rush.
We all turned to stare at Mr. Kobayashi's face.
It was deathly pale, his eyes wide with shock.
His mouth opened as if to say something, but we heard nothing, as if watching a silent film.
What is it?{r}{p}Are you about to start another joke?”
Kyoko said, laughing, but as she studied Mr. Kobayashi's expression, her laughter stiffened.
Mr. Kobayashi swallowed hard and finally found his words.
Uncle, honestly…{r}{p}I'm not falling for it.”
I just went there, and he was in pieces in the room!”
